consensus_summary: Blind consensus treats the new moon primarily as an OT ceremonial month-beginning observance in Israel’s appointed calendar, whose distinctively Christian meaning is typological: a shadow fulfilled in Christ (Col 2:16–17), with secondary associations of renewal, eschatological worship, or empty ritual.
book_summary: The book identifies the new moon as the “renewed moon,” i.e. the full moon that marks the start of the month, appears in the east gate, and functions as the sign of the appointed times, explicitly against the common dark-conjunction/first-crescent view.
consensus_core_identification: Ceremonial month-beginning appointed time (shadow of Christ / renewal motif).
book_core_identification: The full moon (“renewed moon”) as the phase that begins the month, located in the east gate, as sign of the appointed times.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus (and the book’s own common-view note) takes the new moon as the dark conjunction or first visible crescent that opens the lunar month; the book reassigns the name and the month-start role to the full moon and ties it to the east gate.
material_contradiction: Full moon and conjunction/crescent are distinct lunar phases; the same ceremonial “new moon” cannot be both the mid-month full moon and the month-inaugurating dark/crescent phase. Accepting the book’s referent replaces the standard one presupposed by the consensus readings.
rationale: Reduced cores conflict on the identity of the referent itself, not merely on typology or devotional emphasis. Consensus symbolism assumes the ordinary biblical-calendrical new moon (month start at conjunction/crescent) and then reads it as shadow/renewal; the book’s entry defines the new moon as the full moon in the east gate. That is a replaced astronomical-calendrical referent (DIFFERENT_REFERENT), hence DIVERGENT rather than a boundary refinement of the same object. Overlap in cited themes (appointed times, worship, Col 2) does not salvage core equivalence.
strongest_objection: The printed texts establish new-moon worship, the east-gate opening on the new-moon day (Ezek 46), and the shadow wording (Col 2), but none equate “new moon” with the full moon or make the full moon the month-starter; standard lunar usage keeps full moon mid-month.
